sender.en: A copy of a real bank or investment firm

name.en: Fake bonds and fixed-term deposits from a “clone” of a real firm

how.en: Professional-looking ads or unsolicited calls and emails offer bonds or fixed-term deposits with attractive rates. The scammers copy the name, address and sometimes the registration details of a real, authorised firm and use look-alike websites and email addresses. A fake adviser asks for your ID, may quote real bond codes and fake regulation, and has you transfer money, often to an account abroad. The money is gone.

text.en: An ad, call or email offers a bond or fixed-term deposit from a well-known firm.
The rate is better than what your own bank offers.
You are told the offer closes soon.
You are asked to send money to an account, often outside Ireland.

Further to our call, please find attached the brochure for the 24-month Fixed Rate Bond at 7.1% AER. To reserve your allocation before the tranche closes on Friday, return a copy of your passport and transfer the deposit to our custodian account in Lithuania. Kind regards, Private Client Desk

An offer you didn’t ask for, by phone, email or online ad.
A payment account abroad or in a different name from the firm.
A website or email address slightly different from the real firm’s.
Check the firm on the Central Bank registers and contact it only through the details listed there.
Never send money to an account the firm’s registered details don’t match. Get independent advice first.
Report it to the Central Bank and to the Gardaí; call your bank if you paid.
